title: “EDUCATION AND HOUSING SCHEMES FOR STS IN KERALA”
body_text:
Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed today in Lok Sabha that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs implements the following five ongoing scholarship schemes for Scheduled Tribe (ST) students across the country, including the State of Kerala. The annual family income limits prescribed under the guidelines of these schemes are as under:
S. No. Name of Scheme Annual Family Income Limit 1 Pre-Matric Scholarship for ST students (Class IX and X) Rs. 2.50 lakhs 2 Post Matric Scholarship for ST students (Class XI and above) Rs. 2.50 lakhs 3 National Scholarship for Higher Education for ST students (Top Class) Rs. 6.00 lakhs 4 National Fellowship for Higher Education for ST students (NFST) No Income Limit 5 National Overseas Scholarship for ST students (NOS) Rs. 6.00 lakhs
Apart from this, 'National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC), under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, an apex organisation set up exclusively for economic development of Scheduled Tribes, extends concessional loans to the eligible Scheduled Tribe persons for undertaking any income generation activities/ self-employment including education loan through its implementing agencies across the country including the state of Kerala. In case of individuals, having annual family income not exceeding ₹ 3 lakh p.a. both for rural and urban areas are eligible for availing concessional loans under the NSTFDC schemes.
In addition to above education support provided by the Central Government, as informed by the State Govt. of Kerala, it is also running its own Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme under which benefit is provided to all eligible ST students without any prescribed criteria of annual family income.
The intervention of housing under PM JANMAN scheme of this Ministry is being implemented by Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) through PMAY-G scheme. As per the approved norms, there is no prescribed annual income limit for sanctioning of awas to Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTG) beneficiaries. However, there are only two (02) exclusion criteria in respect of PVTG households – (i) household with pucca houses and (ii) Household with any member as a government employee.
Further, housing assistance is also provided by the State Govt. of Kerala through their LIFE Mission. As per the guidelines of the LIFE Mission Scheme, the annual family income ceiling prescribed for availing housing benefits is ₹3.00 lakh.
As per the information received from State Govt. of Kerala, the majority of the Scheduled Tribe population in Kerala belongs to the economically weaker sections. It has not come to the notice of the State Government that a large number of Scheduled Tribe beneficiaries are being excluded from housing schemes on account of the prescribed income limit. In cases where Scheduled Tribe families are not eligible for housing assistance under the LIFE Mission due to prescribed income ceiling, they may be considered for housing assistance under the housing schemes implemented by the Scheduled Tribes Development Department, Govt. of Kerala. With regard to educational assistance, the question does not arise since there is no prescribed annual family income in the State Govt. of Kerala.
The appraisal and approval of the Expenditure Finance Commission (EFC) for their continuation of schemes implemented by M/o Tribal Affairs during F.Y. 2026-27 to 2030-31 is currently ongoing wherein, inter-alia, the proposal to revise the annual family income ceiling is included for seeking the approval of the Dept. of Expenditure on the draft EFC. The decision regarding enhancing the annual income limit under the said schemes in the EFC is subject to the approval of the Competent Authority.
RN/
*****

enrichment.summary: In a Lok Sabha reply, MoS Tribal Affairs Durgadas Uikey detailed the income-eligibility limits under five central ST scholarship schemes (Pre-Matric, Post-Matric, Top Class, NFST, NOS) and NSTFDC concessional loans, along with housing support under PM JANMAN/PMAY-G for PVTGs and Kerala's own LIFE Mission and state scholarship schemes. He noted that a proposal to revise the income ceilings is under EFC appraisal for FY2026-31, pending Department of Expenditure approval.
enrichment.context: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs runs multiple scholarship schemes to support Scheduled Tribe students at different educational stages, most of which impose annual family income caps (except NFST) to target economically weaker beneficiaries. NSTFDC, the apex financial institution for ST economic development, provides concessional loans including for education and self-employment, also subject to income limits. On the housing front, PM JANMAN (launched for PVTGs) routes its housing component through PMAY-G with no income ceiling but only two exclusion criteria, reflecting a policy shift towards near-universal coverage for the most vulnerable tribal groups. Kerala supplements central schemes with its own income-criteria-free scholarships and the LIFE Mission for housing, which does have a ₹3 lakh income ceiling, though the state clarifies alternate housing schemes exist for those excluded. The mention of an ongoing Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) appraisal for scheme continuation (2026-31) with a proposal to revise income ceilings indicates potential policy recalibration to widen eligibility, relevant to inclusive welfare planning for STs given rising costs of living and inflation-adjusted eligibility criteria.

prelims_questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding scholarship schemes of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs for Scheduled Tribe (ST) students: 1. The National Fellowship for Higher Education for ST students (NFST) has no annual family income limit. 2. The Post Matric Scholarship for ST students has an annual family income limit of ₹6 lakh. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, NFST has no income limit, while Post Matric Scholarship has an income limit of ₹2.50 lakh, not ₹6 lakh (which applies to Top Class and National Overseas Scholarship).

prelims_questions.question: The PM JANMAN scheme, whose housing component is implemented through PMAY-G, is primarily targeted at which of the following groups?
options: All Scheduled Caste households below poverty line
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that the housing intervention under PM JANMAN is implemented for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTG) beneficiaries through PMAY-G, with no income limit and only two exclusion criteria.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the rationale behind prescribing income ceilings in welfare schemes meant for Scheduled Tribes. Critically examine whether such ceilings help or hinder the objective of inclusive development, with reference to central and state-level ST welfare schemes.
Examine the significance of PM JANMAN scheme in addressing the housing and developmental needs of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) in India.
